title: Career Roadmap— B.Sc. Cloud Computing / Big Data Analytics → Cloud Support Associate
summary: A Cloud Support Associate helps customers and internal teams troubleshoot cloud infrastructure, applications, connectivity, access, storage, and deployment issues. The role combines IT fundamentals, cloud-platform knowledge, systematic problem-solving, and clear technical communication.

facts.Current degree: B.Sc. Cloud Computing / Big Data Analytics

blocks.text: A Cloud Support Associate helps customers and internal teams troubleshoot cloud infrastructure, applications, connectivity, access, storage, and deployment issues. The role combines IT fundamentals, cloud-platform knowledge, systematic problem-solving, and clear technical communication.

With a B.Sc. in Cloud Computing or Big Data Analytics, you can target entry-level positions such as Cloud Support Associate, Cloud Operations Trainee, Technical Support Engineer — Cloud, or Junior Cloud Operations Analyst. Your eligibility will depend on the employer's requirements and your practical skills.
What you will do

items.text: Troubleshoot cloud virtual machines, storage, networking, and access issues.
Investigate application errors, service availability, and performance problems.
Review logs, monitoring alerts, and configuration settings.
Support identity and access management, backups, and security controls.
Document incidents, communicate updates, and escalate complex issues.
Help customers or engineering teams restore services and prevent recurring incidents.

blocks.text: Core platforms
AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud
Technical foundations
Linux, networking, IAM, storage, monitoring
Essential strengths
Troubleshooting, documentation, customer communication
Career directions
Cloud engineering, DevOps, SRE, cloud security, data platforms

Learn the fundamentals shared across platforms before going deep into one provider. Your first role usually benefits more from solid troubleshooting than from superficial familiarity with all three major clouds.
1. AWS Cloud Support
Learn EC2, S3, VPC, IAM, CloudWatch, DNS, security groups, and basic load balancing. This path suits cloud infrastructure and support roles that use AWS.
2. Azure Cloud Support

Learn Azure virtual machines, storage accounts, virtual networks, Microsoft Entra ID, Azure Monitor, and role-based access control. This is useful for organizations operating Microsoft-based environments.
3. Google Cloud Support
Learn Compute Engine, Cloud Storage, VPC networking, IAM, Cloud Logging, and BigQuery fundamentals. This can suit cloud operations or data-platform support teams.

blocks.label: Recommended starting point
blocks.text: Pick one platform—AWS or Azure is a practical starting choice—and learn it through hands-on labs. Add a second platform later if the roles you target require it.
This plan assumes a three-year undergraduate programme. Adapt it to your university syllabus and the time remaining before graduation.
Year 1
Foundations
Build IT and networking fundamentals

items.text: Learn computer hardware, operating systems, and basic Linux commands.
Study IP addressing, DNS, DHCP, routing, ports, HTTP/HTTPS, and VPN concepts.
Learn Python fundamentals, SQL basics, Git, and command-line tools.
Understand virtualization, servers, storage, and cloud computing concepts.
Practise diagnosing common connectivity and operating-system issues.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Set up a Linux virtual machine, document its configuration, and troubleshoot simulated network and service problems.
Year 2
Cloud operations
Learn the selected cloud platform

items.text: Create and manage virtual machines, storage resources, and virtual networks.
Learn IAM, roles, policies, security groups, and least-privilege access.
Practise logs, metrics, alerts, backups, and basic incident investigation.
Understand load balancing, DNS configuration, availability, and recovery.
Use Python or shell scripts for routine administrative tasks.
Learn the basics of databases, data pipelines, and analytics if your degree emphasizes Big Data.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Deploy a small cloud-hosted application and document how you would diagnose a failed service, connectivity issue, or permission error.
Year 3
Job readiness
Build operational experience and a portfolio

items.text: Learn structured troubleshooting, incident priority, escalation, and service-level agreements (SLAs).
Practise Linux service management, log analysis, and basic performance diagnostics.
Use infrastructure-as-code fundamentals such as Terraform where appropriate.
Explore containers and Docker, then learn the basics of CI/CD.
Complete a cloud monitoring or incident-response project.
Prepare for cloud support interviews and apply for internships and entry-level roles.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Present a cloud project with an architecture diagram, security configuration, monitoring evidence, troubleshooting guide, and cost-control measures.
Prioritize skills in this order. You do not need to master every cloud service before applying.

For cloud support roles, projects should demonstrate that you can deploy, monitor, secure, and troubleshoot infrastructure—not simply create a cloud account.
Project 1 — Deploy a Cloud-Hosted Web Application

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Beginner
Deploy a simple Python or static web application on your chosen cloud platform. Configure access, networking, and basic monitoring.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Architecture diagram, deployment steps, access configuration, and a troubleshooting guide.
Project 2 — Cloud Monitoring and Incident Investigation

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Intermediate
Set up monitoring for a test workload. Create a threshold alert, inspect logs, simulate a safe failure, and document how you diagnosed and resolved it.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Metrics and log screenshots, incident timeline, root-cause analysis, and prevention recommendations.
Project 3 — Secure Cloud Environment

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Intermediate
Create a small test environment with separate user roles, restricted network access, and appropriate logging. Test what each role can and cannot access.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Permissions matrix, security configuration, test results, and remediation notes. Never publish credentials or secrets.
Project 4 — Cloud Cost and Resource Audit

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Job-ready portfolio
Inventory resources in a test account, identify idle or unnecessary services, estimate costs, and configure a budget alert where available.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Resource inventory, cost-control plan, cleanup checklist, and documented lessons learned.

blocks.label: Recommended capstone
blocks.text: Build a small cloud-hosted application with monitoring, least-privilege access, a backup plan, and a troubleshooting runbook. Demonstrate at least three scenarios: an application failure, a permission error, and a connectivity issue.

blocks.label: Cost and safety note
blocks.text: Cloud services can incur charges. Use free-tier offers only after checking their current terms, set budget alerts, avoid exposing public access unnecessarily, and delete resources after testing.
Start with one cloud platform and choose a certification aligned with your target roles. A certification can support your resume, but practical troubleshooting skills remain essential.

blocks.text: If your degree emphasizes Big Data Analytics, also develop SQL, data-processing fundamentals, and basic knowledge of managed data services. These skills can support a later move into cloud data engineering.
Start applying when you can troubleshoot basic Linux and networking issues, explain cloud fundamentals, and demonstrate at least one working cloud project.

blocks.text: Where to look in India

Research cloud service providers, IT consulting firms, managed service providers, SaaS companies, and enterprise infrastructure teams. Examples of employers to investigate include AWS, Microsoft, Google Cloud, TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech, Accenture, and Cognizant. This is a list of potential employers to research, not confirmation of current openings.
Weekly application routine
Read job descriptions carefully. Some positions focus on customer-facing support, while others require Linux administration, coding, or production infrastructure experience.

rows.text: A virtual machine is unreachable. What do you check?
Instance state, network routes, firewall rules, IP configuration, DNS, and service status
What is the difference between object and block storage?
Explain common storage use cases and access patterns
Identity, authentication, authorization, roles, policies, and least privilege
An application is slow. How do you investigate?
Metrics, logs, resource utilization, dependencies, and recent changes
What is the difference between a public and private subnet?
How would you handle a critical support ticket?
Assess impact, follow incident procedures, communicate updates, document actions, and escalate
How do you control cloud costs?
Resource inventory, budgets, utilization, and cleanup of unused resources

blocks.text: Practise explaining your troubleshooting process step by step. In support interviews, a clear, safe diagnostic method is often more valuable than guessing a solution immediately.

rows.text: Service troubleshooting, ticket handling, platform fundamentals
Independent incident resolution and resource management
Senior Cloud Engineer / Site Reliability Engineer
Cloud Architect / Platform Lead / Cloud Operations Manager
Architecture, technical strategy, or team leadership

blocks.text: These stages are indicative. Progression depends on hands-on experience, specialization, employer needs, and demonstrated technical ability.
Days 1–30
Foundations
Learn Linux, networking, Python basics, and cloud concepts. Set up a safe lab environment and practise troubleshooting connectivity and service issues.
Days 31–60
Cloud practice
Deploy a small application, configure access and monitoring, and document how you would diagnose failures. Learn one provider's core services in depth.
Days 61–90
Job readiness
Complete a troubleshooting-focused capstone, prepare your resume, practise support scenarios, and apply for internships and entry-level cloud support positions.

blocks.label: Final recommendation
blocks.text: For a B.Sc. Cloud Computing / Big Data Analytics graduate, prioritize Linux, networking, IAM, cloud storage, virtual machines, and monitoring. Pick one cloud platform, complete a troubleshooting-focused project, and practise explaining how you diagnose incidents. Once you have a strong foundation, expand into cloud administration, DevOps, cloud security, or data engineering based on your interests.
